description: Finds the served model for a real thing described in plain words, such as "a lithium cell discharging in the cold". It returns the best few cards and solvers, each with fit first (the words that matched, and model_of: the one real thing it is a model of, and its range) and then accuracy: against_measurement, the evidence behind it in one of three words, as list_cards and list_solvers give it ("compared with measurement", "held to a reference calculation" or "company specimen"); compared_with, what it was fitted on; and accuracy_against_measurement, what it was compared with outside the fit, within what, and the gap, in numbers. Fit and accuracy are separate: a model with a gap is still the served model of its thing. The names it gives (domain and card, or solver) are the names list_cards and list_solvers give and the names describe_card, describe_solver, cite and every other tool take; describe_card or describe_solver gives the range and every refusal. When nothing served fits it says so, having compared every card and solver, names the nearest by words and why they are not it, or says that there is no near one, and says where requests for a model go. A model is set aside when the description names another thing of its kind (another gas, another maker's cell, another planet's probe). It is matched against a fixed list of terms with no model call: the same words give the same answer.
